evidence.title: Peculiar places 100-day moratorium on data centers
evidence.supports: Establishes the 100-day moratorium's Monday vote (internally dated to 2024-08-19) and its Nov. 27, 2024 natural end date; describes it as unanimous and precautionary pending further research/zoning changes.
evidence.quote: PECULIAR - The Peculiar Board of Aldermen voted unanimously Monday evening to place a 100-day moratorium on data centers, not accepting plans, reviewing, permitting, etcetera during this period. ... The moratorium will end on Wednesday, Nov. 27, at which time the Board could vote to extend it if more time is needed.

evidence.title: Peculiar reverses zoning for data center after cries from neighbors
evidence.supports: Confirms the Board of Aldermen's same-day unanimous vote to remove the data-center definition from the light-industrial zoning ordinance, superseding the moratorium with a permanent fix; describes the project as a 500-acre, multi-building hyperscale facility.
evidence.quote: City leaders in Peculiar, Missouri, listened to its citizens on Monday night and blocked a major data center from coming into the small community. The data center would have spanned across 500 acres with multiple buildings right next to several homes and businesses. ... Peculiar originally approved the zoning for it by adding a 'data center' definition into the existing light industrial zoning code. The Board of Alderman reversed that decision on Monday by removing the definition from the ordinance.

decisions.notes: MAJOR FINDING: current_status/outcome were previously unconfirmed; this is not simply an expired 100-day pause -- the city permanently removed data centers from its zoning code on 2024-10-21 after a roughly 1,000-resident opposition campaign (about one-sixth of the city's population), so enacted_status should move from 'expired' to 'replaced'. The Planning and Zoning Commission tabled the proposed permanent ban on 2026-02-09 (6-2 vote). The April 13, 2026 P&Z agenda packet (downloaded 2026-04-29) lists TA-2026-01 as the first public hearing item with a recommended motion to forward approval to City Council; City Council Resolution R26-007 (passed 2026-03-17) requested that P&Z commit to voting on TA-2026-01 at its April 2026 meeting and the staff memo schedules the City Council public hearing for 2026-05-05.
